newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power holds ahead of milder weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power holds ahead of milder weekend.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity values in the southeastern U.S. were steady to slightly higher Friday in sparse trading, stalled by a weak cooling demand in most of the region, industry sources said.

"It's getting warmer. No one is trading," said one power marketer, referring to the return of more seasonable temperatures to the Southeast this weekend following the cold spell experienced earlier in the week.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Friday delivery was talked steady in the $23.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) area.
Firm, off-peak electricity for next-day delivery was also stable in the $15.50-16.00 range, but no deals could be confirmed done.

In the northern portion of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) system, small volumes of firm, peak electricity traded around $20.00 for Saturday, $18.50 for Sunday and about $19.00 for Monday, as compared to Thursday's $17.00-$18.00 trading range.

TVA was offering its own generation for next-day sale today, but the volumes were limited due to the uncertainty surrounding the restart of its 1,148 megawatt (MW) Sequoyah nuclear unit 2, according to market sources.
TVA would not comment on restart of the unit, but the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said the unit would likely be on line this weekend.
"Things will come back down next week if Sequoyah comes back up," said one power trader, adding the return of a Florida nuclear unit brought more power to the market.
A number of nuclear plants returned to the grid Friday, including Georgia Power's 1,162 megawatt (MW) Vogtle nuclear unit 2 and Florida Power and Light's 666 MW Turkey Point nuclear unit 4.

In addition, Virginia Power's 911 MW North Anna nuclear unit 1 is expected to return to full power on Saturday after Thursday's shutdown. The adjacent unit, with a generating capacity of 909 MW, is expected to return to 100 percent of capacity Sunday.
Temperatures are expected to be much above-normal next week in the Southeast, the National Weather Service reported, which may attract more buyers to the market to meet air-conditioning demand.
